_comment: Template for runtime/providers.json (gitignored). Copy it, pick a default profile, and put the KEY IN THE ENVIRONMENT — api_key inline is refused. The key may also live in ~/.config/cyboros/<profile>.env (mode 600, KEY=value or export KEY=value); the environment wins. Cloud profiles need allow_cloud=true here and --allow-cloud on the run, which also connects at launch.
_capabilities: A profile declares what its endpoint accepts and local/adapters.js consumes ONLY that. Keys: tool_calls (native|text), tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls (bool|null), reasoning {param,on,off}, reasoning_field (reasoning_content|reasoning|null), reasoning_echo_with_tools, strict_unknown_fields, grammar, timings, stream_options, sampling_extras, context_window_tokens, reserved_output_tokens, context_safety_tokens, max_output_tokens, pricing {input_per_1m,output_per_1m,cached_input_per_1m}. An unknown key is refused at load time, not ignored. Types differ only in defaults: openai-compatible is the bare chat-completions shape (every optional field OFF unless declared), llama-cpp adds the llama.cpp extensions this project uses (grammar, timings, sampling_extras), deepseek assumes a strict cloud endpoint. An unsatisfiable request — a GBNF grammar on a profile that never declared one — is an error, not a silent downgrade.

capabilities._note: openrouter/auto has no single window: a window number here would be a guess. Pin a model and set context_window_tokens; until then the legacy context_char_budget below is a ~15k slice.

type llama-cpp already turns on grammar/timings/stream_options/sampling_extras; naming them again would only repeat the type's defaults. chat_template_kwargs is llama.cpp-only and is sent because THIS profile declares it, never to a cloud endpoint. context_window_tokens must match your llama-server -c.

pricing._note: peak rates, the safe direction for a budget; off-peak is half. Verify against your account.

capabilities._note: Overridable defaults, not gospel. What this profile claims: thinking toggled with thinking:{type}, reasoning arriving in reasoning_content and echoed back when tools are present, a 1M window with 384K max output, and strict field handling. NONE of it was verified with a live call from this repo — no API key, no request. To replace this paragraph with evidence: `node tools/provider-probe.js plan` then `run --max-requests 24 --yes`; the record applies only to the same base_url|model. What it deliberately does NOT claim (and therefore never sends): chat_template_kwargs, grammar, timings, top_k, stream_options, parallel_tool_calls, tool_choice. Change any key here and the next request follows; delete the block and you get the openai-compatible defaults.
